taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO as Chrysactinia mexicana A.Gray.
look_here_first: Crush-free visual ID starts with the tiny narrow leaves: damianita is a low woody-based subshrub with many very narrow aromatic gland-dotted leaves and solitary bright-yellow heads held above the canopy on slender peduncles.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural flora. Williamson — UT PRC detailed county treatment. Kerr — Kerr WMA flora with voucher.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Habitat association from Joey is supporting context; county PASS is based on independent records.

best_field_traits: evergreen aromatic subshrub with woody lower stems
many short linear to linear-oblanceolate leaves
leaves conspicuously oil-gland dotted under magnification
solitary terminal radiate heads on slender peduncles
bright yellow ray florets surrounding yellow disc florets
involucre with relatively few phyllaries and conspicuous oil glands
inferior ovary maturing into a cypsela
morphology_keys.family_training: Good Asteraceae whole-plant-to-head lesson: aromatic/gland-dotted narrow foliage gets you close, then involucre, ray/disc florets and cypsela/pappus confirm the composite structure.
morphology_keys.video_training: Joey shows the whole plant and flower heads in thin limestone habitat and mentions aromatic foliage and Tageteae.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Damianita is a low woody-based aromatic subshrub with numerous tiny linear gland-dotted leaves; Tetraneuris linearifolia is an annual herb with a different involucre/pappus pattern.
